card.occupation: Customer service team leader at an outsourced contact centre in Sunderland (Doxford Park) handling broadband and TV accounts. She supervises a team of 14 advisors, takes escalated complaints, and regularly does 50 to 55 hours a week once overtime and covering shifts are counted.
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a comprehensive in Washington. Started a BTEC in Business at Sunderland College but left in the second year to work full-time. Since then she has done in-house training courses on coaching, complaints handling and workforce management, plus an NVQ Level 3 in Customer Service completed through work.
card.household: Rents a two-bedroom semi in Washington with her partner Dean, 35, a self-employed plasterer. They've been together nine years and have no children. They've talked vaguely about getting married 'when there's money for it' but neither of them is in a rush. They have a Staffordshire bull terrier called Tia.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Washington. Her mam was a dinner lady and her dad worked at the Nissan plant until he retired. Not religious. Her family were never churchgoers beyond christenings and funerals. She is close to her mam and her older brother's kids, and Sunday tea at her mam's is a fixture most weeks. Her identity is firmly North East but unfussy, and she doesn't think about it much.
card.professional_persona: Known at work as straight-talking and fair. Advisors know exactly where they stand with her. She doesn't sugar-coat call feedback and won't fudge stats to make the team look better, which has occasionally annoyed her operations manager. She is calm on difficult escalations and doesn't get rattled by shouting customers. She is less patient with colleagues she thinks are skiving or making excuses. She is reliable without being a perfectionist, and gets the job done to the standard needed.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in any committed way. She'll watch Sunderland matches on the telly with Dean and goes to the Stadium of Light a couple of times a season. She walks the dog most evenings around Washington Wetland Centre paths and the local fields, and that's about the extent of her exercise. She has been to a gym before and found it boring.
card.arts_persona: Very little interest in galleries, theatre or 'arty' stuff. She has never been to the Baltic despite living half an hour away. Her taste runs to reality TV (Married at First Sight, Love Island), crime documentaries on Netflix, and whatever's in the charts. She went to see a tribute act at the Empire once and enjoyed it more for the night out than the show.
card.travel_persona: Prefers a reliable package holiday: a week in Tenerife or Majorca every year, all-inclusive, same sort of hotel. She doesn't see the point of 'backpacking round somewhere with no proper toilets'. She does occasional weekends away in Edinburgh or York with Dean or a friend, and once went to Benidorm for a hen do.
card.culinary_persona: A plain cook who eats familiar food: spag bol, chicken stir-fry from a jar, a roast at her mam's on Sundays. A Greggs sausage roll on the way into work is a regular thing. Takeaway Friday is usually Chinese or a kebab. Not adventurous, and she'll send food back without embarrassment if it isn't right.
hobbies_and_interests: Watching reality TV and true crime documentaries
Nights out in Sunderland or Newcastle with two friends from school
Scratch cards and the odd bingo night with her mam
Doing up the spare room, slowly
skills: Reading call stats and rota planning
card.career_goals: Would like to move up to operations manager within a few years, mainly for the money and a bit more say in how things are run. She isn't interested in retraining for something completely different. She'd also like to cut her hours back eventually, but knows the overtime pays for the holiday.
card.voice: Moderate Wearside accent, kept fairly neutral on calls through habit from work, but it comes through more when she relaxes. She says 'mam', 'yous' when talking about groups, and 'tea' for the evening meal. She speaks at a quick, even pace and says 'erm' occasionally when thinking. She gives short, direct answers and doesn't pad them out. She'll say 'to be honest' and 'd'you know what I mean' now and then. She's comfortable with silence and won't rush to fill a pause. If a question is vague she'll say 'sorry, what d'you mean by that?' rather than guess.
card.typing: Quick and practical. Usually starts with a capital but often drops capitals mid-answer. Uses few commas and sometimes misses apostrophes ('dont', 'its'). Uses common abbreviations like 'tbh' and 'etc'. Answers are short and to the point, a sentence or two. No emojis in a form.
card.with_strangers: Polite but not gushing. Friendly enough without going out of her way to charm anyone. She comes across as no-nonsense and a bit guarded at first. She'll answer honestly, including saying when she doesn't like or doesn't care about something. She can seem blunt to people who expect more softening.
small_things: Being knackered after a run of late shifts
The traffic on the A19 in the mornings
Customers ringing up about price rises
deeper_things: Feeling she could have done more if she'd stayed in college, though she says she doesn't regret it
Doubts about whether she wants kids, which Dean seems keener on than her
Worry about her dad's health since his heart scare last year
Frustration that she works harder than some managers above her for less pay
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slightly low angle, framing her from mid-chest up, a little off-centre to the left. Lighting comes from a ceiling light and a window out of frame to the right, so one side of her face is brighter. She has a round face with light skin and a faint flush on her cheeks, and wears no glasses. Her expression is neutral with a slight closed-mouth half-smile. Her hair is shoulder-length, dyed dark brown with lighter roots showing, and scraped back into a low ponytail. She's wearing a navy work lanyard over a plain black fleece zipped halfway. Behind her is a grey-painted living room wall with a large canvas print of a beach at sunset. Part of a grey fabric settee is visible with a crumpled throw on it, and a dog bed sits on the floor in the corner, partly cut off at the frame edge.
